name: Tatara Tales
description: Something ominous seems to have occurred at Inazuma's Tatarasuna...

steps.description: Activate the Kamuijima Cannons and destroy the rifts
Activate the Kamuijima Cannons and destroy the rifts
Activate the Kamuijima Cannons and destroy the rifts
Get close to the Mikage Furnace
Take a picture of the storage device
Ask the two about the situation
Ask the two about the situation

dialogs.content: It's hopeless...
Hello, are you Xavier?
#That's right! Xavier's the name and the name's mine! But is it fate fair or foul that we should meet at this time and place? Pray tell, fine {F#lass}{M#lad}, who are you?
I'm just a helpful adventurer.
Adventurer? Ah, a grand adventurer, en route to the stars, the abyss, and beyond, arrives here on the island of conflict and Tatarigami!
On the way here, did you happen to see a protective cover that looks like... a bubble?
No, I didn't.
Oh... Okay then. No, that makes sense, the containment dome's not usually visible — if you want to view it from a distance, you have to employ a specific observation technique...
So how do you do it?
Not with my eyes, that's for sure. I... "view" it by availing myself of this work: the "Mikage Furnace Emergency Response Procedures (Trial Version)."
I've followed the instructions to the letter. Based on the readings given by the instrument, it seems that the dome has been successfully activated.
Ah, one other thing I should mention is that, technically speaking, its official name is the Mikage Furnace Emergency Containment Dome.
Now, as for the Mikage Furnace—
Miyuki already explained.
Fantastic! She is a considerate and capable young lady. Ah, what a blessing it is to become acquainted with one such as her.
But whatever happens, I've now sealed it following the Mikage Furnace Emergency Response Procedures (Trial Version), so the problem is almost certainly contained, to a certain extent...
"To a certain extent"?
Well, it might be 893 pages long, but the trial version has no information on the emergency measures applicable in a wartime scenario...
We need to form an editors' group for a Trial Version: Expanded Edition (1st Issue) and have a detailed discussion on additional emergency scenarios...

Anyway, point being, even though I have followed the emergency response measures, they aren't the most complete... and the environment within the containment dome has turned... hmm... less than ideal, shall we say.
The Mikage Furnace has now ceased operation indefinitely, and that soldier is getting incredibly antsy about it.
Allegedly, Miyuki recently borrowed some of his people to arrange for the evacuation of the civilians. Now that really got him riled up, hahaha...
But if things continue like they are, who knows. Tatarasuna might just turn into a glorious firework visible all the way from my dear home, the beautiful town of Petrichor...
When you say "firework"...
In the worst-case scenario, yes, it could. We've not yet reached that stage, but if it gets that serious...
You'll look to the procedures for further guidance?
Precisely! But considering it mostly deals with insurance claims and lawsuits and the like, I was rather hoping it wouldn't come to that.
Recently, though, the instrument is indicating that the containment dome I activated is a little unstable. But I don't know what or where the problem is...
Back in my beautiful homeland of Fontaine, we would normally have a Vision-wielding expert diagnose the problem.
Then, we would form a dedicated review panel to discuss and raise proposals, approve a solution, then organize the remedial work.
But with Inazuma being the way it is right now, all I can do is try to determine what might be going on through naked-eye observations and my imagination.
In short, you're taking a best guess?

#"Best guess"!? {F#My dear girl}{M#My dear boy}, please! That is a woefully inadequate representation of what goes on. A fairer description would be "observation and inference drawing on a wealth of professional experience, including analogous previous cases."
Okay, so an educated guess.
Precisely.

So my... ahem, guess is that it could conceivably... potentially? Possibly? Probably be an issue with the device containing the Tatarigami core that is having a knock-on effect on the containment dome I installed.
But even if that's the case, the readings given by this instrument seem off... Something must have happened outside the dome as well...
So you're just missing your Vision bearer, yes?
Um, yes, that's it. Under the current circumstance, in the area around the Mikage Furnace, only a Vision bearer would be... well, safe.
Anyone else would probably make it around three paces.
Except for me, I'm a special case, haha... I'd have croaked about halfway through taking my first step.
In short, if we only knew what exactly was going on with the Mikage Furnace, I'd likely be able to formulate a repair plan. But we'd still need a review panel to approve it...
Wait, it would only take one person to fulfill the function of a review panel... Aha! So we're all set.
Allow me to take a look.
Huh? But it doesn't look like you have a Vision...
I have my ways.
Is that so... Alright, you've swayed me. It's not technically proper procedure, but we shan't achieve anything by just sitting on the issue.
And I suspect that if we left that soldier to handle it, his report would still be sitting in his superiors' chest of drawers gathering dust as the island was being blown sky-high.
Let me pack up here, then we'll head off. In any event, we need to get closer to the Mikage Furnace to get a better idea of the situation.
Perhaps you could go and investigate the surrounding area while I'm packing up. These strange readings must have something to do with whatever's happening in the Mikage Furnace.
Pack up? Has that been approved by a review panel?
Actually, as representative of the present review panel, I have already granted myself authorization to pack up and strike camp. So no need to worry about that.
I'm no ordinary individual.
I can go investigate for you.
So you're lacking someone capable of investigating?
...could it really get that bad?
Please give me the short version.
...Basically, it's a super-smelter built using Fontaine technology, powered by a Tatarigami core brought over from Yashiori Island.
Due to the impact of the war, the Mikage Furnace is now in an extremely unstable state...
Surely you can't see it either?
I'm here to help out.
To help out, you say? I say, from the looks of your attire, we two are fellow Inazumaphiles on a pilgrimage of passion! A rare pleasure, my friend.
I must say, I am touched by your kind intentions. But I must also apologize for being frank in saying that I don't believe there is any help you can offer...
Phew... The situation looks stable, at least...
The situation with the Mikage Furnace?
Yes indeed. From my observations, the internal build-up of Tatarigami energy doesn't seem too high.
The reason I initially activated the dome was to stop people from going inside. Mostly because of the legal liability it puts on us...
Basically, if too much energy accumulates inside, then this dome is completely usel—
Ahem! Heh... The main thing here is that everything's looking good right now, so it's happy days.
No need to pore over mundane details at this point. So, how is the dome looking?
It's got three rifts in it, and a whole load of Fatui.
Rifts... Wait a moment, F—Fatui? What are those sly Snezhnayans doing all the way out here?
Whatever it is, it can't be good.
You've got that right. But if the current issues with the Mikage Furnace are the Fatui's doing, then that complicates things...
Goodness gracious. How can this be happening!
I'm just a humble engineer. I only wanted to come here to do a little research, do some filming, get a taste of Inazuma's delightful culture, et cetera...
How did I go from that to being caught up in this whole mess!?
It began as a simple technical issue. Then that soldier turned up and all of a sudden it's somehow a process issue!
Then, somewhere during said process, it transforms again into an Inazuman domestic affair that outlanders are strictly prohibited from interfering in.
And now the Fatui are here. If it goes on like this, the nature of this problem is going to change quite radically indeed!
It's all the Fatui's fault.
Ugh... Whatever, I'm here now, and I'm the only person capable of resolving the issue with Mikage Furnace.
Technically, ignoring it would be a compliant decision both in terms of process and in terms of who has jurisdiction over it. But I can't just leave it unresolved.
Perhaps I just need to accept that for a researcher, this is just the way life is... or as we say in Fontaine, c'est la vie!
If the Fatui are really here to try and get their hands on the Tatarigami energy inside the Mikage Furnace, then the containment dome should be a major stumbling block to their plans.
Were those rifts also...

Indeed. There is no doubt in my mind that the Fatui are at least tangentially related to those rifts. Hmm, I see... So it's those cracks in the containment dome that are causing my instruments to give these anomalous readings...
I must say, they are very stealthy. They managed to make it all the way here, damage the dome, and access the inside of the Mikage Furnace without anybody finding out.
The Fatui are good at acting in the shadows.
If that's the case... There's a real possibility here that they've already made it inside...
If they're left to their own devices in there...
Are the Fatui really so reckless? If it exploded, they would share the same fate as everyone else...
I wouldn't put it past them.
Dear me. They are truly... daring. First things first, we must find a way to scare them off.
Give me a moment to think...
I've got it! Since they decided to sneak inside the Mikage Furnace quietly, it must mean that they wish to avoid a direct confrontation with the Shogunate.
So all we need to do is make some sort of big, dramatic gesture to make them think that the Shogunate is already onto them.
That might just make them much more cautious in their approach, which will make our investigation much easier.
"Dramatic gesture"?
Do you know of the Kamuijima Cannon? It's a big gun built using the latest technology, powered by Electro.

The Shogunate had a few of them installed on this island for military purposes, since this is where the front line was. But as the war went on, things changed, and now they're currently sitting there unused.
"Things changed"? What, exactly?
You'd have to ask our soldier friend. But I'm sure he'd only tell you that he's "not at liberty to disclose classified military intelligence."
If you want my take, I think the Shogun's Army underestimated the sophistication of their enemy.
They installed the Kamuijima Cannons hoping to halt Sangonomiya's advance with overwhelming firepower.
But although the Kamuijima Cannon does indeed pack quite the punch, it has a limited field of fire and is not very mobile.
Most importantly, big artillery guns like these need several people to operate them, and maintenance is a real headache.
Trying to defend the Mikage Furnace and the Kamuijima Cannons at the same time meant that our soldier friend and his comrades were spread much too thinly.
So ultimately, it actually gave Sangonomiya an opportunity. After making it past the Kamuijima Cannons' field of fire, they quickly took down the forces guarding the Mikage Furnace.
Before the Shogun's Army could get emergency reinforcements to the Mikage Furnace, they had already withdrawn from there and started attacking from a different direction.
Constantly being dragged back and forth kept the Shogunate's forces fully occupied, so when the Mikage Furnace started having problems, they were forced to halt production.
Meanwhile, the Kamuijima Cannons installed in the wild became essentially useless against the kind of tactics employed by Sangonomiya's side.
Suffice it to say that as far as the fight on this island went, Sangonomiya had the upper hand.
So did Sangonomiya damage the Mikage Furnace?
Hmm, I don't think so. They should be well aware that the Tatarigami sealed inside wouldn't treat Sangonomiya or the Shogunate any differently from each other if the Mikage Furnace was destroyed.
All they want is to continuously harass and attack the Mikage Furnace to be a nuisance to the Shogun's Army and slowly wear them down.
I wonder who it is that is planning all these precise attacks from Sangonomiya's side...
Well, that's enough chit-chat. Whatever the case, the Kamuijima Cannon will definitely cause an unimaginable ruckus, which is just what we need.
And as a result of some miraculous coincidence... I actually know how to operate the cannon...
Does this miraculous coincidence have to do with Fontaine?
Well... Haha... I won't get deeper into it, but we do have other technologies besides just maintaining and producing equipment...
Are you going to fire at the Furnace directly?
As I've said before, the containment dome is meant for stopping people from entering.

The Fatui have already broken through. That much you've seen with your own eyes. Though it may seem like it's just a few small tears... The truth of the matter is that the dome is actually barely holding up.
If they're left unchecked, even if the Mikage Furnace is alright, they'll definitely find other ways to cause problems.
If we don't destroy the dome, we'd have to go through the three tears that the Fatui made to repair the Mikage Furnace.
We'd be fish in a barrel for those Fatui to shoot.
But if we destroyed it altogether, not only would it shock the Fatui and provide us with an advantageous opportunity...
It would also allow for us to have more routes to choose from.
Besides, if we can repair the Mikage Furnace in time, everything will return to normal even if we do destroy the containment dome.
Have a little in faith in me, and in the marvelous technology of my homeland Fontaine.
Come, let me mark the locations of the Kamuijima Cannons for you on your map...
Don't we need to prepare some projectiles?
Normally, we would, and the Cannons use a very special type of projectile.
That's why the Shogunate is so lax about leaving these huge cannons in the wild.
But as I've said before, I happen to know how to operate this sort of cannon. What I also know is how to make use of Electro to bypass our projectile-related limitations...
But since neither of us has a Vision, if we are to get a hold of some stable elemental power...
We should go ask the Treasure Hoarders if we might "borrow" a few of those curious, small bottles in which they seal some...
Don't worry, I can control the elements.
What? But you're not a bearer of the Vision... Hmm, I guess we all have our own little secrets, eh? I shan't pry.
Just leave it to me.
Then on behalf of our special review board, I will be entrusting you with this task. I'm confident that we will make a wonderful team.
What if the containment dome breaks?
It's tech from Fontaine again, isn't it?
I'll go and defeat them right away.
What? Whoa, whoa, hold on a second! That's not what I meant. Hear me out first.
What if they destroy the Mikage Furnace...
The Fatui are good at everything, except doing good.
I sympathize with you...
You've had a similar experience before? Drawn into a messy situation that fundamentally has nothing to do with you whatsoever? That's unfortunate...
Whatever it is, it's connected to the Mikage Furnace.
You really think so? If they're the cause of the issues, that really complicates things...
Goodness me, they don't beat about the bush, do they...
This is how the Fatui roll.
Their lack of care for the delicacies of law are really...
Ah. Well. *cough* The further they are from me, the better.
It seems like their target is Tatarigami energy, which is within the Mikage Furnace.
Go check up on the status of the storage device inside the Mikage Furnace while the Fatui are distracted by all this ruckus we're making.
If you encounter any Fatui, why, take them out.
I have every confidence in your abilities.
Looks like they do have their eyes set on this place.
Did you find the device?
Yes, and I took a picture of it.
Let me take a look... Good, good. it hasn't suffered too much damage.

If all the other emergency systems are working normally, most of the energy circuits inside the device should have been cut off already. That I would consider great fortune, even amidst our many miseries.
Hmmm... I have a few more preparations to make, and I also need to give the problems we face here at the Mikage Furnace some thought...
Come find me after a while. We still have a lot of work to do here.
You're back. My, my, that was loud — my ear drums are still ringing.
After hearing the cannons, the Fatui will most certainly suspect that the Shogunate has become aware of their activities.
Still, something seems off here... why hasn't Tatarigami energy begun to leak out after the containment dome was destroyed?
Could it be that some of the Mikage Furnace's systems are still operational and have already purified some of the energy?
Or perhaps the Fatui are collecting that energy...
Whatever the case may be, please take this opportunity to go and find out...
W—Watch out! It's the Fatui!
Is there something I can help you with?
What's all this "Mikage Furnace" and "Tatarigami" talk?
It's just a small problem. We need a little time to sort out...
You're an adventurer, aren't you? This place isn't suitable for you or your ilk. Get out of here.
*sigh* How did it come to this...
What this "Mikage Furnace" that you guys were talking about earlier?
You're an outlander, aren't you? You've got some terrible luck to have traveled to Inazuma at this time...
That island is called Tatarasuna. It's a smelting plant for Jade Steel, which is used to forge weaponry.
Are you aware of the legends of Inazuman swords?
The Jade Steel manufactured here is the reason that Inazuman swords are as sharp and durable as they are.
So it's a weapon material?
No need to worry, this can hardly be called confidential military intelligence.
After all, the Tenryou Commission feels that having the ability to forge powerful weapons is something they should flaunt.

A few years ago, for the purpose of expanding production capacity, they hired a team of consultants from Fontaine. They built the Mikage Furnace, a machine that can fully harvest the powers of the Tatarigami.
We've warned them countless times not to let their guard down when it comes to the Tatarigami, but they decided to go ahead with the project anyway.
After the Mikage Furnace started production, most of the consultant team returned to Fontaine. Only Xavier, who we just mentioned, stayed behind in Inazuma.
But during one of the previous battles, something went wrong with the furnace. The part that stored the corrupt Tatarigami energy became extremely unstable...
Work was halted in Tatarasuna and everyone was evacuated shortly after.
Xavier took emergency action, and he seems to have set up a containment dome around the Mikage Furnace.
It's only a temporary solution, though. He's probably still on the island now, trying to figure out a way to solve the problem for good.
Meanwhile, the Shogunate is only concerned about restarting production as soon as possible. I hear that they're even considering calling the consultants from Fontaine back again.
But I don't think they'd be willing to come under the current conditions in Inazuma...
And it just has to be that Hanbei guy in charge of this whole thing, doesn't it...
Who's Hanbei?
A... manager, you could say. Always going on about procedures, articles, and applications...
His first reaction is never to find the solution to the problem. Instead, it's about what forms should be filled out, and which powerful individual needs to be informed about the incident beforehand.
He's probably in the city right now preparing to submit whatever forms he can find.
I really don't know if he's actually aware of the severity of the situation...
*sigh* I just hope that Xavier or our craftsmen can find some way to solve the problem.
If something were to go wrong with the Tatarigami inside the Mikage Furnace...
Well, if that happens, you should probably leave the island.
It sounds top-secret...
Eh, it's not that big of a secret.
This all sounds pretty serious.
It'll affect our adventures for sure.
That's true... But didn't she mention that someone named Xavier is trying to find a solution?
Why don't we go and take a look? It'd put our minds at ease if we could help take care of this, wouldn't it?
Oh, won't someone think of the poor treasures?
The Fatui... What are they doing here...
What is it that you're doing in Inazuma?
Well, I came to Inazuma with the consultant team. In truth, I'm just your everyday engineer.
To be honest, my real reason for being here was to shoot a "dokumentari film" on-site at the Mikage Furnace for the purpose of promoting our nation's technologies.
But seeing the furnace's current state, I think it's best if I didn't shoot that film...
What is Fontaine like?
#Ah, my fine {F#lass}{M#lad}, that's a splendiferous question!
Indeed, I often ask myself how I might describe the charm of my country to others, even with my limited knowledge and vocabulary.
Now, what should I speak of first?
For instance, I could tell you of the majestic waterfall that made a deep impression on my soul as I worked in my study in Petrichor.
Or perhaps I could sing the praises of the countless gorgeous maidens in the Court of Fontaine, ethereal as the clouds themselves...
Or the mesmerizing lake that held the reflections of the stars and the moon, such that walking along its banks was like treading amid the celestial skies...
You really do love Fontaine, don't you...
Of course! And I shall tell you more about its wonders once I've found a satisfactory answer to that question of mine.
What are these "films" that you were talking about?
Oh, that? It's something that I discovered when I was researching Kameras.
I made some improvements to the Kamera and turned it into a Film Kamera that is also capable of continuously projecting a string of photos, thus creating moving images.
This technique is still in its preliminary stages and is far from perfect, so I have yet to formally apply for a patent. Not that I really could apply at this point in my current circumstances...
But before I left Fontaine, I heard that some of my colleagues were quite interested in this act of playing back images in sequence... *sigh* I can only hope that they don't act all too quickly...
Why are the Fatui interested in the Tatarigami?
There should be something about this in the "Mikage Furnace Emergency Response Procedures (Trial Version)" somewhere...

Paimon thinks they mentioned something about the Mikage Furnace.
Maybe something's happened to this island! Let's go ask those two over there.

After all, we cannot fix the Mikage Furnace with just two very kind hearts...
On the way here, did you happen to see a protective cover that looks like... a bubble?
Not really.
